data.title: Herpes zoster — viva
data.summary: Viral infections · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Herpes zoster** (Viral infections)_

**Q1. Pathogenesis?**
- Reactivation of latent VZV in dorsal root/cranial nerve ganglia after childhood varicella, triggered by age-related decline in cell-mediated immunity, immunosuppression, stress, trauma; virus travels down the sensory nerve to skin

**Q2. Clinical features?**
- Prodrome of pain/tingling, then unilateral grouped vesicles on erythematous base in a dermatomal distribution not crossing the midline (thoracic commonest, then ophthalmic division of trigeminal); regional lymphadenopathy

**Q3. Signs to remember?**
- Hutchinson's sign: vesicles on tip/side of nose (nasociliary branch) → high risk of ocular involvement
- Ramsay Hunt syndrome: facial nerve palsy + vesicles in ear/palate + vertigo/tinnitus (geniculate ganglion)

**Q4. Complications?**
- Post-herpetic neuralgia (pain >90 days; risk ↑ with age), ocular (keratitis, uveitis, acute retinal necrosis), motor paresis, meningoencephalitis, myelitis, stroke (vasculopathy), secondary infection, scarring, disseminated zoster (>20 lesions outside dermatome) in immunocompromised
- Dermatological: post-zoster granulomas/Wolf isotopic response, pigmentary change, herpes gangrenosum

**Q5. Diagnosis?**
- Clinical; Tzanck (giant cells), PCR of vesicle fluid (test of choice), DFA, culture

**Q6. Treatment?**
- Start within 72 h (later if new vesicles/immunocompromised/ocular): acyclovir 800 mg five times daily × 7 days, valacyclovir 1 g three times daily, famciclovir 500 mg three times daily
- IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg 8-hourly for disseminated/immunocompromised
- Analgesia; ophthalmology review for HZO

**Q7. Treatment of post-herpetic neuralgia?**
- Pregabalin/gabapentin, tricyclics (amitriptyline/nortriptyline), topical lidocaine 5% patch, capsaicin 8% patch, tramadol/opioids, nerve blocks

**Q8. Prevention?**
- Recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix, 2 doses) for adults ≥50 years and immunocompromised ≥18; live vaccine (Zostavax) discontinued in many countries

**Q9. Zoster as a marker?**
- Multidermatomal/recurrent/disseminated zoster in a young person — screen for HIV and malignancy

## Quick spotter facts
- Unilateral dermatomal grouped vesicles — herpes zoster

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Herpes simplex virus chapter — herpes zoster); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.20. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
